**[t1] Nina (facilitator):** Hi Tom, thanks for meeting. Can you explain the vision behind the neighborhood tool lending library?

**[t2] Tom (stakeholder):** We want local residents to borrow lawnmowers, drills, and home improvement tools without needing to buy expensive equipment they only use once a year. Our community volunteers need to track who checked out each tool and when it is due back.

**[t3] Nina (facilitator):** What is the check-out experience you envision when someone comes into the workshop?

**[t4] Tom (stakeholder):** It should work like renting bowling shoes where you just hand over an ID and grab what you need. Zero friction, very informal.

**[t5] Nina (facilitator):** How do you handle maintenance and safety checks for motorized equipment?

**[t6] Tom (stakeholder):** Safety is critical for power equipment. We must record safety inspections before any motorized equipment is reissued to another borrower.

**[t7] Nina (facilitator):** What happens when an item is returned damaged or dull?

**[t8] Tom (stakeholder):** The desk volunteer logs maintenance requests so damaged gear is flagged as out of service until repaired.

**[t9] Nina (facilitator):** How do you want community members to feel when they interact with the tool library?

**[t10] Tom (stakeholder):** Above all, the check-out process should feel warm and welcoming to neighbors rather than feeling like a sterile financial transaction.

**[t11] Nina (facilitator):** What about membership dues or late return fees?

**[t12] Tom (stakeholder):** We ask for voluntary donations rather than punitive late fees, but overdue tools should trigger polite return prompts.

**[t13] Nina (facilitator):** Who conducts the technical tool refurbishments and blade sharpening?

**[t14] Tom (stakeholder):** Our volunteer repair specialists do all the sharpening and motor tune-ups on Wednesday evenings, although honestly none of the repair volunteers have been interviewed yet about what workshop tools they need.

**[t15] Nina (facilitator):** Are tool manuals and operation instructions made available to borrowers?

**[t16] Tom (stakeholder):** Borrowers should receive basic safety guidelines and manufacturer operating instructions when taking high-risk tools.

**[t17] Nina (facilitator):** Is there any seasonal peak in equipment requests?

**[t18] Tom (stakeholder):** Spring gardening season brings huge demand for tillers and aerators, so waitlists for high-demand equipment will become necessary.
